# Model-Based Analysis



## Customer Segmentation
```{python}
# Select relevant features for clustering
data_bases = data.select([
    'price',
    'total reviewers number',
    'sales',
    'accommodates',
    'host total listings count'])

```

```{python}

def create_pipeline(num_clusters, random_seed = 42):
    """
    Creates a machine learning pipeline with a scaler and KMeans.
    """
    pipeline = Pipeline([
        ('scaler', StandardScaler()),
        ('kmeans', KMeans(n_clusters=num_clusters, random_state=random_seed))
    ])
    return pipeline


```

Define a function to calculate the total within-cluster sum of squares and plot the elbow graph.

```{python}
def calculate_totwithinss(data, k):
    kmeans_pipeline = create_pipeline(k, random_seed=10)
    kmeans_pipeline.fit(data)
    return kmeans_pipeline['kmeans'].inertia_

#My code kept throwing an error so I asked chatGPT what was wrong with it, it told me to drop the nulls from my dataset
data_bases_clean = data_bases.drop_nulls()
# Calculate tot.withinss for different values of k
k_values = range(1, 10)
totwithinss_values = [calculate_totwithinss(data_bases_clean, k) for k in k_values]

# Create a DataFrame for results
kmeans_results = pl.DataFrame(
    {'num_clusters': k_values,
     'tot_withinss': totwithinss_values})

# Plot the elbow method using Plotly Express
elbow_plot = px.line(
    data_frame = kmeans_results,
    x = 'num_clusters',
    y = 'tot_withinss', 
    markers = True,
    labels = {
        'num_clusters': 'Number of Clusters', 'tot_withinss': 'Total Within SS'
        },
    title = 'Elbow Method for Optimal k')

elbow_plot.show()
```

```{python}
# Choose the number of clusters based on the elbow method
optimal_k = 2

#again had to ask Chatgpt why I'm getting a strange error
data_bases_clean = data_bases.drop_nulls()
# Run K-means clustering

data_kmeans_pipeline = create_pipeline(optimal_k)
data_kmeans_pipeline.fit(data_bases_clean)


# Add cluster assignments to the original data
data_with_clusters = data_bases_clean.with_columns(
    pl.Series(
        "segment_number",
        data_kmeans_pipeline['kmeans'].labels_ + 1
        ).cast(pl.Utf8).cast(pl.Categorical)  # Make cluster labels 1-indexed
)

data_with_clusters.head()
```

```{python}
# Calculate summary statistics for each segment
segment_summary = data_with_clusters.group_by('segment_number').agg(
    [
        pl.mean('price').alias('mean_price'),
        pl.mean('sales').alias('mean_sales'),
        pl.mean('accommodates').alias('mean_accommodates'),
        pl.len().alias('n')
    ]
)

segment_summary

##Segment 1 contains the majority of listings which are more expensive and generate higher sales. These listings contain higher accodomations or rooms, so listings with more rooms are more popular.
```
